cpu_budget: workload pinned to CPUs 0-7 (8 cores, identical for old controls and new datasets); monitor pinned to CPU 9

collection_settings.native: perf record -e cycles:u -F <rate> -g --call-graph dwarf,16384 wrapping the runner; rate 99 Hz for PDF configs, 49 Hz for XLSX configs
collection_settings.pyspy: py-spy record --subprocesses --rate <rate> --format raw (99 Hz PDF / 49 Hz XLSX), separate run from perf
collection_settings.syscalls: strace -f -c, separate run, only for configs where listed

roi: samples from the runner '[scene/dataset] start:' stdout line (emitted after pre-run validation+probe, before the loop) to process end; pre-run hash validation, environment probe, interpreter checks and recipe load are excluded. The runner's own per-loop workspace reset, step scheduling, business verifier read and summary writes are inside the ROI (they were part of the old workload measurements too).
repeats: native configs: two independent container runs; py-spy configs: one independent run each (repeat variability therefore unavailable); stat and syscalls once per configured dataset

configs.note: matches the old 3-repeat N=10 weight measurement
1 loop per run, 2 independent runs; avoids unnecessary long TLC repetition while matching old 49 Hz caliber

record_count_note: PDF N=1 comparisons target the ANALYSIS-python3123 claims (collected on the single-applicant version, 10 rounds); PDF N=10 comparisons target the REPORT-pdf10-weight claims (3 repeats). Percentages are never mixed across scales.
